SEM images of core-shell electrospun fibers washed by methanol for 24 h (left) and methanol for 5 min (right). Fibers were generated using similar electrospinning parameters as mentioned above, though the flow rates for the core & shell solutions were varied in order to improve the silica loading within the electrospun fibers. An early batch of fibers demonstrated that there were problems during the electrospinning using the flow rates of 0.07 mL/min for the core and 0.035 mL/min for 27 the shell, which would correspond to a theoretical loading of about 80% silica in the fibers. When viewing the fiber samples under SEM, bundles of SBA-15 would appear on the carbon tape, as shown in Figure 22a. This indicated some problems occurring during the electrospinning process with those operating conditions, though fibers were still being produced. In order to make the pores of the embedded SBA-15 accessible, different washing conditions were tested to determine an appropriate method of removing PEO to move forward with. Samples of the fibers shown in Figure 22a were washed by placing the fibers in a vial of methanol and keeping them in an oven at 65oC for either 19 or 72 h. After the wash, fibers were dried in an oven at 65oC overnight and the masses were tracked to determine if the washes were successful by maintaining a weight within 5% of expectations. Fiber samples were then evaluated for their pore characteristics via 77K N 2 porosimetry. Figure 22b demonstrates that both time lengths for washing the fibers were successful in making the pores of SBA-15 accessible, as seen by the available pore volume centered around SBA-15’s characteristic pore width of ~100 Å. The shorter time length was selected for future washes as the longer time was not necessary to reveal more available pores. Figure 22. An early batch of fibers a) viewed under SEM and b) demonstrating available pore volume after washing by 2 different methods. With the concern of SBA-15 not entirely becoming embedded in the fibers, new protocols were developed when making the fibers and fabrication conditions were held constant. The flow rates for both the core and the shell solutions were set to 0.07mL/min, leading to a theoretical silica loading of 60% in the fibers. The new protocols involved a thorough cleaning of the entire spinneret between runs and checking on the fibers to ensure that there was no clogging happening during the electrospinning process. A new batch was obtained and viewed under SEM as shown in Figure 23a, showing that the SBA-15 was no longer appearing spread out on the carbon tape and it was now embedded in the fiber structure. The pore characteristics of this sample were measured by 77K N porosimetry and the pore size distribution is provided in Figure 23b, revealing 2 that the SBA-15 was truly embedded in the structure and that the washing procedure worked.
